status: POST-HOC analysis specification locally recorded before calculating the new aggregation-control results.
registration: Not preregistered and not unseen confirmation: these saved datasets and their original arithmetic-mean outcomes were already available and inspected.
question: On exactly the same saved five fixed-binding responses, how do normalized geometric probability averaging and original arithmetic probability averaging compare? The original canonical first order is retained as a lower-cost reference.
motivation: Aggregation-only control inspired by log-probability averaging; not an AnyJev reproduction. Token-to-semantic-option binding, prompts, candidate sets, orders, model outputs and candidate normalization stay fixed. No permutation-dependent token rebinding, prior correction, null prompt or additional inference is introduced.
scope: All four model/dataset strata reported separately. The same 480 distinct questions are reused across two models; no pooled accuracy, independence assumption across models, or causal language/family attribution.

methods.first_order: Replicate 0 in the frozen logical order, regardless of randomized physical execution order. Use saved candidate-normalized probabilities.
methods.arithmetic_mean5: a_k = (1/5) sum_r p_rk, using the saved candidate-normalized probabilities with option_0..4 semantic alignment. Identical to the original five-member arithmetic ensemble.
methods.geometric_mean5: g_k = exp((1/5) sum_r log p_rk) / sum_j exp((1/5) sum_r log p_rj). Compute log p from saved finite logits with stable log-softmax at T=1, avoiding clipping and probability underflow. Verify saved probabilities against reconstructed softmax using the frozen reader. At fixed binding and T=1 this equals softmax of the mean candidate logits; verify that identity independently for each question.

prediction_ties: First index in canonical option_0..4 order, matching the original reader. Record exact top-score tie counts.

outcomes.accuracy: Correct count and fraction for all three methods.
outcomes.paired: For every contrast report question-paired accuracy difference, reference-wrong/alternative-correct, reference-correct/alternative-wrong, both correct, both wrong, and label disagreements (including wrong-to-different-wrong).
outcomes.diagnostic: Mean and maximum total variation between arithmetic and geometric distributions, with all item predictions/probabilities retained in records.jsonl. This is a distribution-change description, not a calibration result.

uncertainty.method: Paired whole-question nonparametric percentile bootstrap within each stratum; resample the same question indices across all three methods. Predictions are fixed; no refit, selection or aggregation tuning.
uncertainty.randomization: Separate random.Random(seed + stratum_index) generators; stratum order models outer, datasets inner.
uncertainty.interval: 95% percentile interval with linear interpolation at positions (B-1)*0.025 and (B-1)*0.975; report valid/invalid draw counts.
uncertainty.interpretation: All intervals are exploratory and unadjusted. No p-values, multiplicity-adjusted winner claim, population equivalence claim, or replacement of original prespecified results. All positive, negative and null findings retained.

cost.accounting: Arithmetic and geometric methods use exactly the same 1200 physical responses per stratum; their costs are not added together. First-order is a 240-response lower-cost reference, not a same-budget competitor. Record input-token and serial-latency sums from the reused members, never interpret these as new timing or online speedups.

exclusions_and_failures: No exclusions, new item selection, retries, sample expansion, policy tuning or new inference. Fail on any manifest, schedule, identity, finiteness, normalization or member completeness mismatch.
limits: Already-seen public validation panel; pretraining exposure unknown.
One Japanese and one English commonsense five-choice task; unequal-size model families and different datasets confound causal comparisons.
One original machine; numerical code checks are not independent human or machine replication.
This isolates only the aggregation rule with the original fixed binding; it cannot establish effects of AnyJev token reassignment or prior correction.
